quote: If a third party claims or threatens a claim that Materials or Base Components IBM provides to Customer or uses in connection with the performance of the Services infringe that party's patent, trademark, copyright, or trade secret, then IBM will indemnify, defend and hold harmless the Customer, its Enterprise and their respective employees, officers, agents and directors against that claim or threatened claim at IBM's expense
rationale: Section 8.1 sits at our fallback position and is therefore acceptable without redline. IBM expressly defends and indemnifies Bluefly and its Enterprise against third-party claims that IBM-provided Materials or Base Components (i.e. the deliverables and hosted components used to perform the Services) infringe patent, trademark, copyright or trade secret rights, and pays awarded damages, costs and reasonable attorneys' fees. The exclusions are the usual ones permitted at fallback — Customer-provided items incorporated into the Materials (p0092), Customer modifications (p0093), and combination/use with non-IBM products, data or apparatus (p0095) — and the remedy ladder is the customary procure-continued-use / modify / replace with functionally equivalent items, followed by a refund credit of amounts paid for the affected Materials or Base Components (p0091). On the super-cap element, the bargain is better than fallback: Section 9.1(a) carves indemnification payments under Section 8.1 out of IBM's $100,000 / twelve-month damages cap entirely, so the IP indemnity is uncapped rather than limited to 3x annual fees. Standard procedure (prompt written notice, IBM control, Customer cooperation with reimbursement of cooperation costs) is present. Preferred-only items fall short and are noted rather than flagged: no indemnity for IBM's breach of law, IBM-caused data breach, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct; the refund credit is capped at twelve months of applicable charges; prompt notice is drafted as a strict condition rather than one qualified by material prejudice; and our indemnity in 8.2(a)3 reaches Services Recipient claims "related, directly or indirectly, to the Services", which is broader than Customer content and breach of law (partly mitigated by the 8.2(c) carve-back for IBM's fault). None of these defeats the fallback, and the walk-away triggers (no Vendor IP indemnity, or a one-way Customer indemnity) are not present.

No survival tails, expense language or extraneous procedures were added. Intent is preserved: the two-category Materials structure, IBM's delivery obligation, the Type I allocation and the data-protection/instructions sentences all survive without contradiction; no undefined terms or dangling cross-references are created. verification.notes: Fallback checklist is complete: the single inserted sentence pair supplies the annual frequency cap, the 15-day notice condition and the 10% cost-shifting threshold in operative language, not merely in the margin comment. Minimal: nothing outside the three fallback parameters was added or deleted; the existing warranty-investigation right, IBM's 11.3(a)/(b) remedies and the emergency notification carve-out are all retained verbatim, and no survival tail, expense language or procedure was bolted on. Preserves intent: the insertion attaches conditions to the investigation right only; IBM's remedial actions under 11.3(a)/(b) and the emergency/legal-requirement exception to pre-action notification continue to operate, and no cross-reference or defined term is left dangling. Optional hardening (not required at fallback): if the counterparty pushes back on a 15-day wait before investigating suspected AUP breaches, consider carving out investigations conducted in an emergency while keeping the cost allocation intact, rather than conceding the frequency cap.
